[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Victor Alade, Tax Manager (senior).
Tax manager: runs the return workflow, the review queue, the extension list, and the R&D credit study. First escalation point for every tax question in the building.
Personality: Fast, organized, keeps three lists and trusts none of them. Protective of his staff's evenings outside season.
Email register: Efficient; bullets when more than two items; signs 'V'.
Chat register: Quick, direct, occasionally emoji-punctuated.
Working hours: 08:00-18:00

[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Depreciation treatment for new equipment purchase

Gabriel,

We’re finalizing the purchase of a new CNC machining center (approx. $480k, placed in service this quarter). I need your read on the correct depreciation method and class life for our tax filings—bonus depreciation vs. straight-line, and any Section 179 limits we should consider given our 2024 income projections.

Please confirm the class life (I believe 7-year MACRS, but want to be sure) and whether we can take 80% bonus this year. Also, flag any state conformity issues that might affect our Illinois return.

We need to lock the fixed asset schedule by Friday. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow afternoon if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Depreciation treatment for new equipment purchase

Dana,

Thanks for the quick note. Confirming our path forward on the CNC machine:

- Class life: 7-year MACRS is correct for the machining center.
- Bonus depreciation: 80% is available for 2024 placed-in-service property.
- Section 179: We can take the full $420k (including installation) via Section 179—this is the primary path given your income projections. Bonus is the fallback if you want to preserve future-year deductions.
- State conformity: Illinois conforms to federal bonus depreciation, but has its own Section 179 cap. I'll reconcile the difference in the state return—no action needed on your end now.

Could you confirm your final sign-off on the Section 179 path? Also, I’ll have the cash-flow comparison (179 vs. bonus) to you by Thursday so we can lock the schedule by Friday.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon if you want to walk through it live.

V

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Victor Alade, Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Re: Depreciation treatment for new equipment purchase — final confirmation

Victor, Gabriel,

Victor — appreciate the added detail, but I need to flag a discrepancy before we lock the schedule Friday.

You’re citing $420k (including installation) for Section 179, while Gabriel and I have been working with the full $480k purchase price. My understanding is that installation costs are included in the depreciable basis for MACRS, but Section 179 applies to the total placed-in-service cost, not a reduced figure. Please confirm the exact basis we’re using — if there’s a legitimate reason to exclude $60k, I need that in writing before Friday.

Also, your note on Illinois conformity contradicts what Gabriel provided earlier. Gabriel indicated Illinois does NOT conform to bonus depreciation but does allow Section 179 up to the federal limit. You’re saying Illinois conforms to federal bonus but has its own Section 179 cap. That’s a material difference for our state return — can you two align on the correct treatment and send me one consolidated answer?

Given the Friday deadline, I need this resolved by tomorrow afternoon. Please coordinate and reply with a single, agreed-upon position, including the cash-flow comparison you mentioned, Victor. If you want to talk it through live, I’m available tomorrow after 2 PM.

Thanks,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

[[ ## intent ## ]]
Confirm final depreciation decision with Dana and Gabriel, request cash-flow comparison deadline adherence, and lock in Friday sign-off path.

Weekly tax huddle: return queue on track, 3 extensions due Thu, R&D one-pager Thu, 3Q margin confirmed, Loop & Ladder scope chat times proposed.
Confirms no additional adjustments in Victor's queue for the line item; validates Gabriel's breakdown (1.2-pt variance from late-Sept material spike, freight immaterial), provides 3Q margin and projection assumption, and confirms no further action needed pending tomorrow's walk-through.
Sends the promised one-page R&D credit summary (FY20–FY22) and proposes two call times for deeper detail, while also offering to discuss the unrelated unbilled overage.
Confirms Section 179 for full $420k CNC machine (incl. installation) as primary path, bonus depreciation as fallback; requests Gabriel's cash-flow comparison by Thursday and confirms no change to Q3 capex forecast.
